notes.note: There is no stable, official, site-by-site public table of UWA rangers. Organisation-wide figures in 2025–26 journalism and speeches cluster around ~3,000 total staff and a previously cited ~2,000 rangers for the whole estate, with density ~1 per 22 km². Recruitment of several hundred to 1,300 rangers was underway in 2025–26. Any number you write next to Bwindi or Pian Upe today will be wrong next quarter. Use the Known ranger / LE notes column only as a qualitative flag.

Working km² is the figure most often repeated in UWA, Wikipedia/WDPA and UN List compilations. Variants are in the notes column. Karuma, Bugungu, Lake Mburo and Toro-Semliki are the noisiest. Always prefer a current gazettement instrument or UWA GIS extract for legal work.

UWA says 12. This workbook uses: Ajai, Bokora Corridor, Bugungu, East Madi, Kabwoya, Karuma, Katonga, Kigezi, Kyambura, Matheniko, Pian Upe, Toro-Semliki. Older lists add Lomunga or Aswa-Lolim (degazetted / defunct as operational reserves). Do not mix eras.

UWA headline figure is 13. Public inventories do not publish one clean 13-row official table. This sheet lists the units that appear repeatedly (Entebbe, Jinja, Kazinga, Ngamba, Otze, Ziwa, Ntoroko-Kanara, Nyaburogo, Malawa, Mount Kei, UWEC, Lake George-associated, plus a catch-all for Ramsar names). Several overlap parks or forest reserves. Sanctuary area totals are indicative, not cadastral.

Ziwa is Rhino Fund Uganda + UWA on ranch land. Ngamba is a trust / JGI-linked sanctuary under the wildlife-law umbrella. UWEC is an education centre. Karenga CWMA is co-managed with community structures. Counting them as 'UWA manages' is correct at mandate level and misleading at payroll level.

Semuliki National Park ≠ Toro-Semliki Wildlife Reserve. Kyambura Gorge ≠ Kyambura Wildlife Reserve (the gorge sits inside the reserve). Entebbe Sanctuary polygon ≠ UWEC campus. Kazinga Sanctuary ≠ Queen Elizabeth NP, though visitors experience them as one trip.

Bird numbers (350, 450, 600…) are literature/tourism figures, not a single standardised atlas extract dated 2026. Mammal lists are presence-of-notable-species, not census totals. For EIA-grade work use the latest UWA State of Wildlife Resources report and site-specific surveys.

World Heritage: Bwindi, Rwenzori. UNESCO-MAB: Queen Elizabeth, Mount Elgon. Ramsar overlays: Murchison delta, Lake George, Rwenzori, plus many wetlands that are not UWA field stations (Mabamba, Lutembe, Opeta, Bisina, Nabajjuzi, Sango Bay…).

UWA website mandate pages (10 NP / 12 WR / 5 CWMA / 13 WS); Uganda Wildlife Act 2019 ss. 25–33 and definitions; UN List of Protected Areas of Uganda (CWMAs dated 2002 with areas); WDPA / Protected Planet dumps mirrored on ArcGIS Hub and IBAT country profiles; gazettement SI for Karenga (2003); IUCN and UWA chimpanzee strategy annex (hectare figures for some WRs); contemporaneous reporting on Ziwa rhino numbers and Kidepo release (2026); UWA/ED remarks on ranger density (2025); Pulitzer Center conservation-tech reporting (EarthRanger sites).

For an audit-grade version ask UWA Planning & EIA / GIS for the current protected-area shapefile and the latest staff establishment by Conservation Area (Murchison, Queen Elizabeth, Bwindi-Mgahinga, Kibale, Kidepo, Lake Mburo, Mt Elgon, Rwenzori, Semuliki, plus Karamoja reserves). That internal table is the only honest source for rangers-per-site.

records.name: Bwindi Impenetrable National Park
records.areaNotes: WDPA ~329 km²; WH listing often 321 km²
records.habitat: Afromontane rainforest; rugged hills 1,160–2,607 m; one of the richest forest ecosystems in East Africa
records.activities: Mountain gorilla tracking (primary draw); forest walks; birding; cultural visits with Batwa; waterfall trails
records.mammals: Mountain gorilla (largest Uganda population; ~half of remaining mountain gorillas globally shared with Mgahinga/Virunga/Volcanoes); chimpanzee; L'Hoest's monkey; black-and-white colobus; elephant (forest); duiker
records.birds: ~350–360 bird species; African green broadbill, handsome francolin, Grauer's rush warbler
records.floraFauna: High tree and fern diversity; Albertine Rift endemics
records.designations: UNESCO World Heritage Site (1994); Important Bird Area
records.governance: UWA; International Gorilla Conservation Programme partners; community groups
records.tourism: Very high (gorilla permits are a national tourism product)
records.rangerNotes: High-value, high-pressure site; ranger escorts mandatory for gorilla tracking
records.threats: Poaching, disease transmission to great apes, human-wildlife conflict on edges, climate/habitat squeeze
records.notes: Often paired with Mgahinga as the Virunga/Albertine gorilla landscape
records.description: Afromontane rainforest; rugged hills 1,160–2,607 m; one of the richest forest ecosystems in East Africa

records.name: Kibale National Park
records.gazetted: 1993 as NP (Crown Forest 1932; gazetted reserve earlier)
records.areaNotes: Some sources 795 km²; chimpanzee strategy annex ~744 km²
records.habitat: Moist evergreen and semi-deciduous forest with grassland pockets; mid-altitude
records.activities: Chimpanzee tracking and habituation experience (Kanyanchu, Ngogo research); primate walks; Bigodi wetland (adjacent community); birding; night walks
records.mammals: Chimpanzee (Uganda's highest density; 13 primate species including red colobus, L'Hoest's, grey-cheeked mangabey); elephant; bushbuck
records.birds: ~375 bird species; green-breasted pitta is a flagship
records.floraFauna: Exceptional primate diversity — often marketed as Uganda's primate capital
records.governance: UWA; Makerere/Ngogo and other long-term research stations
records.rangerNotes: Research presence supplements monitoring; visitor security focused on forest trails
records.threats: Snaring, crop-raiding elephants, forest fragmentation outside the park
records.notes: Corridors toward Queen Elizabeth via Kasyoha-Kitomi / Kalinzu landscapes matter for elephants
records.description: Moist evergreen and semi-deciduous forest with grassland pockets; mid-altitude

records.name: Kidepo Valley National Park
records.areaNotes: Widely cited 1,442 km² in some UWA materials
records.habitat: Dry savanna, Narus and Kidepo valleys, mountains (Morungole, Lotukei) on South Sudan/Kenya frontier
records.activities: Game drives in Narus Valley; Narus River viewpoints; Kidepo River; cultural visits (Karamojong, Ik); night drives; ostrich and rare dry-country game; 2026 white-rhino release from Ziwa
records.mammals: Elephant, buffalo, Rothschild's/Nubian giraffe, lion, leopard, cheetah, bat-eared fox, greater and lesser kudu, eland, zebra, hartebeest, oribi; black-backed jackal; ostrich
records.birds: ~475 bird species; kori bustard, secretarybird, carmine bee-eater, ostrich
records.floraFauna: One of Uganda's most intact large-mammal assemblages; dry-country specialists absent from western parks
records.designations: Important Bird Area; part of Kidepo Critical Landscape
records.governance: UWA; landscape links to Karenga CWMA and South Sudan's Kidepo
records.tourism: Medium and rising (remoteness kept numbers lower than Murchison/QENP historically)
records.rangerNotes: EarthRanger / LE operations cited among UWA's priority parks; remote patrols
records.threats: Poaching, livestock incursions, regional insecurity historically, climate variability
records.notes: Buffer/corridor role of Karenga CWMA is operationally important
records.description: Dry savanna, Narus and Kidepo valleys, mountains (Morungole, Lotukei) on South Sudan/Kenya frontier

records.name: Lake Mburo National Park
records.gazetted: 1983 NP (controlled hunting area / reserve earlier; status changes through 2000s)
records.areaNotes: Wikipedia table 260; some lists 370 km² (older controlled-hunting extent)
records.habitat: Acacia savanna, wetlands, five lakes; mosaic with surrounding Ankole ranches
records.activities: Game drives; boat on Lake Mburo; walking safaris (one of few parks where walking is a core product); horse riding; night drives; birding
records.mammals: Plains zebra, impala (the only Ugandan park with both in numbers), eland, buffalo, hippo, leopard, hyena; sitatunga in wetlands; no lion resident historically (occasional)
records.birds: ~350 bird species; African finfoot, papyrus gonolek, spot-flanked barbet
records.floraFauna: Tight park–ranch interface; wildlife often denser on neighbouring ranches than inside the fence-less mosaic
records.designations: Lake Mburo–Nakivali Ramsar complex nearby / overlapping wetland system
records.rangerNotes: Problem-animal work with surrounding livestock keepers is a large part of the job
records.threats: Encroachment, illegal grazing, hyena/leopard conflict, wetland conversion outside
records.notes: Best example in Uganda of a savanna park embedded in private livestock land
records.description: Acacia savanna, wetlands, five lakes; mosaic with surrounding Ankole ranches

records.name: Mgahinga Gorilla National Park
records.areaNotes: WDPA ~39 km²; Uganda's smallest NP
records.habitat: Virunga volcanoes (Muhabura, Gahinga, Sabinyo); montane forest, bamboo, alpine heath
records.activities: Mountain gorilla tracking (Nyakagezi group and others when ranging on Uganda side); golden monkey tracking; volcano climbs; cave visits; Batwa/Garifuna cultural trails
records.mammals: Mountain gorilla (shared Virunga population); golden monkey; buffalo; elephant (seasonal); giant forest hog
records.birds: Albertine Rift endemics; handsome francolin, Rwenzori turaco
records.floraFauna: Transboundary park with Volcanoes NP (Rwanda) and Virunga NP (DRC)
records.designations: Part of Virunga Massif / Greater Virunga Landscape
records.tourism: High per km² (tiny park, high-value permits)
records.rangerNotes: Small area, intensive visitor management and border coordination
records.threats: Insecurity in neighbouring DRC affects ranging; human pressure on all three volcano slopes
records.notes: Gorillas routinely cross international borders — visitor product depends on that day's ranging
records.description: Virunga volcanoes (Muhabura, Gahinga, Sabinyo); montane forest, bamboo, alpine heath

records.name: Mount Elgon National Park
records.gazetted: 1992 (forest reserve much earlier; transboundary with Kenya NP)
records.districts: Mbale, Bududa, Sironko, Kapchorwa, Kween, Bulambuli
records.areaNotes: Ugandan portion commonly 1,110 km²; the mountain massif is shared with Kenya
records.habitat: Extinct shield volcano; caldera; montane forest, bamboo, heath, afro-alpine; Wagagai 4,321 m
records.activities: Mountain climbing (Sasa, Sipi, Piswa, etc.); Sipi Falls (adjacent); cave systems (Kitum historically, others); community trails; birding
records.mammals: Elephant (small/forest population), buffalo, leopard, hyrax, duiker; primates including black-and-white colobus; no classic savanna game-drive product
records.birds: ~300 bird species; Lammergeier historically, Jackson's francolin, Ross's turaco
records.floraFauna: Giant lobelia and groundsels; caldera wetlands
records.designations: UNESCO-MAB Biosphere Reserve (Mount Elgon); transboundary with Kenya
records.governance: UWA; Kenya Wildlife Service on the other slope; local governments on densely settled foothills
records.tourism: Medium (mountaineering and Sipi more than game viewing)
records.rangerNotes: Boundary and encroachment patrols dominate over anti-poaching of large mammals
records.threats: Encroachment, landslides, high human density on slopes, illegal logging
records.notes: More a mountain/forest park than a Big Five park
records.description: Extinct shield volcano; caldera; montane forest, bamboo, heath, afro-alpine; Wagagai 4,321 m

records.name: Murchison Falls National Park
records.districts: Buliisa, Nwoya, Masindi, Kiryandongo, Pakwach, Oyam
records.areaNotes: Largest NP; WDPA ~3,904 km²; conservation area larger when Bugungu + Karuma reserves are added
records.habitat: Albertine Rift savanna, Nile, delta papyrus, Budongo/Kaniyo Pabidi forest outliers, falls where the Nile drops through a 7 m gorge
records.activities: Game drives (north and south banks); launch trip to the falls and the delta; top-of-the-falls hike; chimpanzee tracking at Kaniyo Pabidi; sport fishing (regulated); birding the delta
records.mammals: Elephant, Rothschild's giraffe (stronghold after translocation programmes), buffalo, lion, leopard, hippo, crocodile, Uganda kob, hartebeest, oribi; chimpanzee in forest sector
records.birds: ~450+ bird species; shoebill in the delta; red-throated bee-eater colonies
records.floraFauna: Murchison Falls themselves are the scenic icon of Uganda
records.designations: Ramsar site (Murchison Falls–Albert Delta); Important Bird Area
records.governance: UWA; oil-development interface in the Albertine Graben; adjacent Bugungu & Karuma WRs
records.tourism: Very high (often Uganda's most-visited savanna park)
records.rangerNotes: EarthRanger hub; large ranger deployment; problem-animal units on the agricultural south and east
records.threats: Poaching, oil & infrastructure, crop-raiding, fires, fishing pressure on the Nile
records.notes: Treat MFNP + Bugungu + Karuma as one conservation landscape in practice
records.description: Albertine Rift savanna, Nile, delta papyrus, Budongo/Kaniyo Pabidi forest outliers, falls where the Nile drops through a 7 m gorge

records.name: Queen Elizabeth National Park
records.aliases: QENP; Queen Elizabeth; includes Kyambura/Ishasha sectors in visitor language
records.areaNotes: Park proper ~1,978–2,056 km²; adjoining Kyambura and Kigezi WRs extend the QE landscape
records.habitat: Rift valley, explosion craters, Kazinga Channel, Lakes Edward & George, Ishasha riverine forest, Kasenyi plains
records.activities: Game drives (Kasenyi, Ishasha tree-climbing lions); Kazinga Channel launch; Kyambura Gorge chimps (in adjoining reserve); crater lakes; birding; Mweya peninsula
records.mammals: Lion (incl. tree-climbing Ishasha population), elephant, buffalo, hippo, Uganda kob, giant forest hog, leopard, chimpanzee (Kyambura), sitatunga
records.birds: ~600 bird species — among the richest parks in Africa; flamingo at crater lakes seasonally; martial eagle, shoebill rare
records.floraFauna: UNESCO-MAB Biosphere Reserve; Lakes George/Edward Ramsar connections
records.designations: UWA; fishing villages inside/adjacent (Katwe, Kazinga, etc.) create a rare inhabited-park pattern
records.tourism: Major LE centre at Mweya / Katunguru; high visitor-security workload
records.rangerNotes: Poaching, human settlements and fishing enclaves, oil exploration history, disease (carnivores), fires
records.threats: Kyambura WR and Kigezi WR function as buffers; do not double-count them as the park
records.description: Rift valley, explosion craters, Kazinga Channel, Lakes Edward & George, Ishasha riverine forest, Kasenyi plains

records.name: Rwenzori Mountains National Park
records.areaNotes: WH listing often 996 km²; chimpanzee annex ~995 km²
records.habitat: Highest mountain range in Africa (Margherita Peak 5,109 m on Mt Stanley); ice, afro-alpine, giant lobelia, montane forest
records.activities: Technical and trekking routes (Central Circuit, Kilembe, etc.); peak bagging; birding in the forest belt; cultural Bakonzo visits
records.mammals: Forest elephant, chimpanzee, Rwenzori colobus, Rwenzori duiker, hyrax; large mammals sparse at altitude
records.birds: Albertine Rift endemics; Rwenzori turaco, handsome francolin, scarlet-tufted malachite sunbird
records.floraFauna: Glaciers in retreat; unique afro-alpine flora
records.designations: UNESCO World Heritage Site (1994); Ramsar (Rwenzori Mountains)
records.governance: UWA; Rwenzori Mountaineering Services and other concession trekking operators
records.rangerNotes: Mountain rescue and trail-head security more than classic anti-poaching
records.threats: Climate change (glacier loss), encroachment at lower contours, trail erosion, insecurity on DRC side
records.notes: Transboundary with DRC's Virunga / Rwenzori sector
records.description: Highest mountain range in Africa (Margherita Peak 5,109 m on Mt Stanley); ice, afro-alpine, giant lobelia, montane forest

records.name: Semuliki National Park
records.aliases: Semliki NP; SNP (not the Toro-Semliki Wildlife Reserve)
records.areaNotes: Distinct from Toro-Semliki Wildlife Reserve (542 km² savanna) immediately to the east/south
records.habitat: True lowland Guinea–Congo rainforest reaching East Africa; hot springs; Semliki River (DRC border)
records.activities: Forest walks (Kirumia trail); hot springs (Bumaga, Sempaya — 'male' and 'female' springs); birding; primate walks
records.mammals: Forest elephant, buffalo, eight primate species including dryas/galago and mona / Dent's mona associations; hippo and crocodile on the river
records.birds: ~440 bird species including 35+ Guinea–Congo biome species found nowhere else in East Africa (e.g. lyre-tailed honeyguide, yellow-throated nicator)
records.floraFauna: Hot springs are a geothermal/cultural attraction as much as a wildlife one
records.designations: Important Bird Area; Albertine Rift / Congo Basin transition
records.tourism: Low–medium (specialist forest/birding park; few general safari visitors)
records.rangerNotes: Small staff relative to remote forest; border issues
records.threats: Encroachment, logging pressure, flooding, DRC-border dynamics
records.notes: Do not confuse with Toro-Semliki Wildlife Reserve — different habitat, different product
records.description: True lowland Guinea–Congo rainforest reaching East Africa; hot springs; Semliki River (DRC border)

records.name: Ajai Wildlife Reserve
records.areaNotes: Also cited 166 km²
records.habitat: Nile-bank grassland, woodland, swamp on the west bank of the Albert Nile
records.activities: Nature walks, birding; historically a white-rhino sanctuary — rhinos were extirpated; restoration interest continues
records.mammals: Uganda kob, oribi, bushbuck, warthog, primates; historically northern white rhino (gone)
records.birds: Strong birding site for West Nile waterbirds and woodland species
records.floraFauna: Floodplain / Nile wetland mosaic
records.rangerNotes: Small reserve; limited tourism infrastructure
records.threats: Poaching, agricultural encroachment, loss of the original rhino population
records.notes: Often discussed in the same breath as Ziwa because of the rhino history
records.description: Nile-bank grassland, woodland, swamp on the west bank of the Albert Nile

records.name: Bokora Corridor Wildlife Reserve
records.areaNotes: WDPA ~1,828 km²; one list erroneously gives 2,056 ha — that figure is wrong by an order of magnitude
records.habitat: Open Karamoja savanna and seasonal wetland (Loporokocho / Opeta system nearby); corridor function
records.activities: Limited formal tourism; game viewing where secure; birding; corridor between Pian Upe and Matheniko / Kidepo landscapes
records.mammals: Oryx historically, zebra, hartebeest, oribi, buffalo, ostrich, lion and cheetah in low numbers; Rothschild's giraffe remnant / recolonisation potential
records.birds: Karamoja dry-country and wetland birds; Lake Opeta Ramsar is adjacent
records.floraFauna: Key part of the Karamoja wildlife landscape
records.designations: Near Lake Opeta / Bisina Ramsar sites
records.governance: UWA; Karamoja local governments; pastoral communities
records.rangerNotes: Vast area, thin ranger coverage; part of Karamoja LE challenge
records.threats: Pastoral conflict, poaching, charcoal, climate, settlement
records.notes: Functionally one landscape with Matheniko WR
records.description: Open Karamoja savanna and seasonal wetland (Loporokocho / Opeta system nearby); corridor function

records.name: Bugungu Wildlife Reserve
records.areaNotes: Sources range 336–520 km²; chimpanzee annex 336 km²; tourism sites often 473 km²
records.habitat: Savanna–woodland buffer on the south-west of Murchison Falls NP; rift-flat toward Lake Albert
records.activities: Game drives as an extension of Murchison circuits; birding; community visits
records.mammals: Uganda kob, oribi, buffalo, elephant moving through from MFNP; hippo toward Albert
records.birds: ~240 bird species cited in tourism material
records.floraFauna: Buffer / corridor for Murchison
records.designations: Part of the greater Murchison conservation area
records.tourism: Low as a standalone product; visitors usually tick Murchison
records.rangerNotes: Covered by Murchison Falls Conservation Area staffing
records.notes: Do not treat as isolated from MFNP
records.description: Savanna–woodland buffer on the south-west of Murchison Falls NP; rift-flat toward Lake Albert

records.name: East Madi Wildlife Reserve
records.areaNotes: Commonly ~829–831 km²
records.habitat: Woodland and savanna on the east bank of the Albert Nile; former conflict-affected landscape
records.activities: Emerging tourism; walking and game viewing developing from a low base; birding
records.mammals: Elephant (recovering), buffalo, hartebeest, Uganda kob, hippo, crocodile; lion in low density
records.birds: Nile–woodland bird community
records.floraFauna: Important recovering northern range after decades of insecurity
records.rangerNotes: Historically understaffed; security context improving
records.notes: Sometimes omitted from short tourism lists but counted in UWA's 12
records.description: Woodland and savanna on the east bank of the Albert Nile; former conflict-affected landscape

records.name: Kabwoya Wildlife Reserve
records.areaNotes: Consistently ~87 km²
records.habitat: Lake Albert escarpment grassland and woodland; rift views
records.activities: Game drives, lakeshore walks, sport fishing on Albert (licensed), birding; lodge-based tourism
records.mammals: Uganda kob, buffalo, warthog, waterbuck; hippo and crocodile on Albert; lion occasional
records.birds: Rift / Albert waterbirds and savanna birds
records.floraFauna: Oil-region reserve
records.rangerNotes: Small reserve, concession-style protection
records.notes: Often paired with Kaiso-Tonya CWMA along Lake Albert
records.description: Lake Albert escarpment grassland and woodland; rift views

records.name: Karuma Wildlife Reserve
records.areaNotes: Sources 574–826 km² (675 / 720 / 826 all appear); chimpanzee annex 574 km²
records.habitat: savanna and woodland on the east of Murchison; Karuma Falls on the Victoria Nile
records.activities: Mostly a conservation / corridor reserve rather than a standalone safari circuit; Karuma Falls viewing; hydropower overlay
records.mammals: Elephant, buffalo, Uganda kob moving with the Murchison system; primates in riverine forest
records.birds: Nile and woodland birds
records.floraFauna: Hydropower dam sits in / beside the reserve
records.designations: Part of greater Murchison conservation area
records.governance: UWA; UEGCL / dam operators as a major neighbour
records.rangerNotes: Covered with MFNP conservation-area command
records.notes: Karuma Falls are on the Nile just upstream of Murchison
records.description: savanna and woodland on the east of Murchison; Karuma Falls on the Victoria Nile

records.name: Katonga Wildlife Reserve
records.areaNotes: Consistently ~207–212 km²
records.habitat: Katonga River wetlands, acacia woodland, papyrus
records.activities: Walking safaris, canoeing, birding; sitatunga-focused product; low-volume exclusive feel
records.mammals: Sitatunga (flagship), waterbuck, bushbuck, buffalo, warthog; chimpanzee reported in riverine forest patches
records.birds: Papyrus and woodland specialists; African finfoot possible
records.floraFauna: Wetland antelope reserve
records.rangerNotes: Small ranger post; walking product needs escorts
records.notes: Best known for sitatunga, not Big Five
records.description: Katonga River wetlands, acacia woodland, papyrus

records.name: Kigezi Wildlife Reserve
records.areaNotes: WDPA ~267 km²
records.habitat: Hilly rift savanna and woodland on the south-east of Queen Elizabeth; Ishasha approaches
records.activities: Usually visited as an extension of QENP / Ishasha; game drives; birding
records.mammals: Uganda kob, buffalo, elephant overflow from QENP, bushbuck, leopard
records.birds: Albertine / rift savanna birds
records.floraFauna: Buffer to Queen Elizabeth NP
records.rangerNotes: Staffed as part of QE conservation area
records.notes: Not the same as Mgahinga / Bwindi highland parks
records.description: Hilly rift savanna and woodland on the south-east of Queen Elizabeth; Ishasha approaches

records.name: Kyambura Wildlife Reserve
records.areaNotes: ~154–157 km²; gorge itself is only a fraction of the reserve
records.habitat: Savanna buffer east of QENP plus the 100 m-deep Kyambura (Chambura) Gorge riverine forest
records.activities: Chimpanzee tracking in the gorge ('Valley of the Apes'); gorge walks; game viewing on the escarpment
records.mammals: Chimpanzee (isolated gorge community), colobus, vervet, elephant and kob on the flats, hippo in the river
records.birds: Forest and savanna mix; good birding in the gorge
records.floraFauna: Classic QE add-on product
records.designations: Functionally part of QE visitor circuit
records.rangerNotes: Gorge visits are escorted; reserve is a QE satellite
records.threats: Genetic isolation of the chimp community, edge pressure
records.notes: Gorge ≠ reserve: the gorge is the feature, the reserve is the 157 km² box
records.description: Savanna buffer east of QENP plus the 100 m-deep Kyambura (Chambura) Gorge riverine forest

records.name: Matheniko Wildlife Reserve
records.areaNotes: WDPA ~1,769 km²
records.habitat: Semi-arid Karamoja plains, rocky hills, Acacia–Commiphora
records.activities: Very limited tourism infrastructure; dry-country game and birding; cultural Karamojong landscape
records.mammals: Lesser kudu, oribi, dik-dik, giraffe remnant potential, ostrich, lion/cheetah scarce; greater kudu reported historically
records.birds: Dry-country larks, bustards, raptors
records.floraFauna: Paired with Bokora as Matheniko–Bokora
records.rangerNotes: Thin coverage over a huge area
records.threats: Armed pastoralism legacy, poaching, drought, settlement
records.notes: Treat with Bokora and Pian Upe as the Karamoja reserve block
records.description: Semi-arid Karamoja plains, rocky hills, Acacia–Commiphora

records.name: Pian Upe Wildlife Reserve
records.areaNotes: Uganda's largest wildlife reserve; ~2,304 km² widely cited
records.habitat: Open grassland, seasonally flooded plains, Mount Kadam on the skyline; cheetah country
records.activities: Game drives (growing product), walking, Kadam climbs, cultural visits, birding; Space for Giants partnership for recovery
records.mammals: Cheetah (one of Uganda's last viable ranges), zebra, eland, hartebeest, oribi, buffalo, ostrich, lion, leopard; roan historically
records.birds: Karamoja / wetland-edge birds; nearby Opeta system
records.floraFauna: Highest-profile reserve in Karamoja after Kidepo NP
records.designations: Important Bird Area landscape; near Ramsar lakes
records.governance: UWA; Space for Giants and other recovery partners
records.rangerNotes: EarthRanger listed among UWA roll-out sites; still under-staffed for the acreage
records.threats: Poaching, charcoal, settlement, livestock competition, climate
records.notes: Largest WR; recovery is a UWA priority
records.description: Open grassland, seasonally flooded plains, Mount Kadam on the skyline; cheetah country

records.name: Toro-Semliki Wildlife Reserve
records.aliases: Semliki WR; Toro Semliki; not Semuliki NP
records.areaNotes: Commonly 542 km²; some GIS 388 km² (different boundary versions)
records.habitat: Rift-floor savanna and woodland between Lake Albert, the Rwenzori foothills and Semuliki NP
records.activities: Game drives, Lake Albert views, chimpanzee tracking in riverine forest (where habituated), birding, cultural visits
records.mammals: Uganda kob, elephant, buffalo, waterbuck, chimpanzee, lion in low density, hippo, crocodile
records.birds: Shoebill possible in Albert flats; good general rift birding
records.floraFauna: Oldest continuously recognised reserve in the set
records.rangerNotes: Separate from Semuliki NP command though neighbouring
records.notes: Name collision with Semuliki National Park is the most common visitor confusion in Uganda
records.description: Rift-floor savanna and woodland between Lake Albert, the Rwenzori foothills and Semuliki NP

records.name: Amudat Community Wildlife Management Area
records.areaNotes: UN List 2,053 km² — the largest CWMA
records.habitat: Semi-arid Karamoja / Pokot pastoral rangeland on the Kenya frontier
records.activities: Community-based wildlife use, cultural tourism potential, corridor toward Pian Upe and Kenya rangelands
records.mammals: Dry-country antelope, ostrich, predators in low density; wildlife shared with Pian Upe system
records.birds: Karamoja dry-country birds
records.floraFauna: Pastoral community land with gazetted wildlife-management overlay
records.governance: UWA guidance + local community institutions / district
records.rangerNotes: Community scouts more than classic park rangers; UWA advisory role
records.notes: People live and farm/graze here legally; this is not a no-settlement park
records.description: Semi-arid Karamoja / Pokot pastoral rangeland on the Kenya frontier

records.name: Iriri Community Wildlife Management Area
